stem: An infection-prevention plan groups patients infected with the same infectious agent in the same room or designated care area. What is this practice called?
rationale: CDC defines cohorting as grouping patients infected or colonized with the same infectious agent together so their care can be confined to one area and contact with susceptible patients can be reduced. Therefore A is correct. Standard Precautions are a separate infection-control framework, and the other terms do not describe this patient-placement strategy.
educational_objective: Define patient cohorting as grouping patients with the same infectious agent in a shared room or care area as an infection-control placement strategy.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Guideline for Isolation Precautions — Glossary and Patient Placement Recommendations
source_locator: Glossary — Cohorting: grouping patients infected or colonized with the same infectious agent together to confine care to one area and prevent contact with susceptible patients; Patient Placement recommendations permit cohorting patients with the same pathogen when appropriate
source_claim_supported: Cohorting is the practice of grouping patients with the same infectious agent together in a shared room or care area to limit exposure of susceptible patients.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

correction_summary: Removed the claim that cohorting is specifically a severe-outbreak or resource-shortage practice and reframed the item around the CDC's exact definition. Replaced weak distractors with other infection/safety terms.
audit_findings: A exactly matches the CDC definition. B, C and D are distinct concepts and do not describe grouping patients with the same infectious agent. No second-answer ambiguity, cueing, or unsupported condition remains.
